title: From Ant to Gradle across ZAP's repositories
description: How the zaproxy, zap-extensions and zap-core-help builds moved from Ant to Gradle in 2019, as recorded in the repository history.

chapters.title: An Ant build from the 1.0.0 era
chapters.text: The very first commit in the repository, titled"Version 1.0.0"(2010-09-04), adds build/build.xml, an Ant build file that marked the start of ZAP's 1.0 release.

chapters.title: Gradle tasks appear alongside Ant
chapters.text: Fast-forward to 2016-07-21: a commit titled"Add Gradle tasks to build/publish zap-2.5.0.jar"adds build.gradle, though the original Ant build file remains alongside it at that point.

chapters.title: zap-core-help sets up Gradle first
chapters.text: On 2019-02-08, zap-core-help gets its first Gradle build, titled"Initial set up to build the add-ons". No Ant build file (build.xml) appears anywhere in that repository's history from that point forward.

chapters.title: zap-extensions drops Ant on 2019-04-03
chapters.text: zap-extensions had depended on an Ant build file since its very first commit back in 2011-12-12. On 2019-04-03, the commit"Remove Ant build and set up Gradle build"removes it and adds the Gradle build. minutes later, the add-ons are relocated into their own projects, one commit each, starting minutes later.

chapters.title: zaproxy follows on 2019-05-22
chapters.text: On 2019-05-22, the commit"Remove Ant build and set up Gradle build"deletes build/build.xml and adds build.gradle.kts. Shortly afterwards,"Add zap project"adds zap/zap.gradle.kts, the module that holds the core sources today.
